title: A Pivotal Safety and Immunogenicity GBS-NN/NN2 Vaccine Maternal Immunisation Trial
official: A Multicentre, Parallel-Group, Observer-Blind, Randomised, Placebo-Controlled, Pivotal Trial Investigating the Safety and Immunogenicity of Group B Streptococcus Vaccine (GBS-NN/NN2) in Pregnant Women and Infants Born to Pregnant Women Vaccinated During Pregnancy
summary:
Main objective: Phase 2: 
To assess the immunogenicity of GBSNN/NN2 Vaccine at birth in infant participants.
To determine the occurrence of SAEs and AESIs after GBS-NN/NN2 Vaccine administration compared to placebo, in both maternal and infant participants.
Phase 3:
To assess the ability of GBS-NN/NN2 Vaccine to induce functional antibody titres protective against iGBS EoD in infant participants.
To assess the ability of GBS-NN/NN2 Vaccine to induce functional antibody titres protective against iGBS LoD in infant participants.
To determine the occurrence of SAEs and AESIs after GBS-NN/NN2 Vaccine administration compared to placebo, in both maternal and infant participants.
conditions: Prevention of Group B streptoccoccus infection
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Carrying a normal singleton pregnancy at 24 (-2/+3) weeks GA at the planned time of the first trial vaccination. GA must be based upon below criteria: • Last menstrual period (LMP) date corroborated by first or second trimester ultrasound examination, i.e., at or before screening. • First or second trimester ultrasound examination only, if LMP is unknown/uncertain.
2. 2. ≥18 to ≤49 years of age with a body mass index (BMI) of >17.5 to <40 kg/m2 (as measured at any  time during the first trimester or just prior to becoming pregnant).
3. 3. Maternal participant having had a foetal anomaly ultrasound examination performed at ≥18 weeks GA with no significant foetal abnormalities observed can be included.
4. 4. Maternal participant or legally acceptable representative (where required for the foetus/infant) who is willing to provide parental consent in accordance with International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) guidelines on Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and local legislation prior to the first dose.
5. 5. Willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, the investigational plan, trial procedures, and intent to deliver at a hospital or birthing facility where trial procedures can be followed.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Having a history of anaphylactic reaction associated with a vaccine.
2. 10. Knowingly carrying, at screening, a malformed or genetically abnormal foetus.
3. 11. Having current pregnancy complications or abnormalities at the time of consent that will increase the risk associated with the participation in and completion of the trial
4. 12. Having had prior pregnancy complications or abnormalities at the time of consent, based on the investigator's judgement, that will increase the risk associated with the participation in and completion of the trial
5. 13. Having a known or suspected immunodeficiency or cancer or a family history of congenital or hereditary immunodeficiency.
6. 14. Having received chronic administration (defined as more than 14 continuous days) of immunosuppressants or other immune-modifying drugs within 6 months prior to the first dose.
7. 15. Having an acute or chronic clinically significant abnormality or poorly controlled pre-existent comorbidities.
8. 16. Having received blood, blood products, plasma derivatives, or any immunoglobulin preparations in the 12 weeks before the first dose or plan to receive such products during the trial.
9. 17. Having a known clinically significant anaemia at time of inclusion per investigator/site staff assessment.
10. 18. Previous vaccination with any licensed or investigational GBS vaccine or planned receipt during participation in the trial (from the first to the last visit).
11. 2. Having a history of allergic reaction (e.g., rash, anaphylaxis) to any component of GBS-NN/NN2 Vaccine
12. 3. Having known syphilis, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and/or active hepatitis B virus (HBV) as assessed by serologic tests conducted during the current pregnancy (for HIV-positive maternal participants, it is acceptable that this was confirmed prior to pregnancy). Maternal participants living with an HIV viral load of <1000 copies/mL and who have been on antiretroviral therapy for at least 3 months prior to screening and are clinically stable may be included.
13. 4. Having a known or suspected infection during current pregnancy with toxoplasma, parvovirus B19, malaria, zika, rubella, varicella, cytomegalovirus, or genital herpes simplex, based on medical history and/or clinical presentation.
14. 5. History of microbiologically proven invasive disease caused by GBS in the current pregnancy (e.g., isolation of GBS from a sterile site: blood, cerebrospinal fluid, or synovial fluid). This does not include asymptomatic bacteriuria or urinary tract infection unless associated with a positive blood culture.
15. 6. Having bleeding diathesis or a condition associated with prolonged bleeding that would, in the opinion of the investigator, contraindicate intramuscular injection.
16. 7. Having any psychiatric condition, including recent (within the past year) active suicidal ideation/behaviour that may increase the risk of trial participation or, in the investigator’s judgement, make the maternal participant unsuitable for participation in the trial.
17. 8. Participated in other trials involving investigational drug(s) or devices within 28 days prior to trial entry, and/or are participating in other trials involving investigational drug(s) or devices, at trial entry or plan to (continue to) participate in other trials involving investigational drug(s) or devices during the trial.
18. 9. Having any lesion or tattoos at the planned injection site (at both arms) that will impair the assessment of the injection site (applicable only for the maternal participants in Phase 2).
